When you ask “Am I am,” you’re touching on a very old question about what it means to exist and to be aware of that existence. In everyday English, the phrase “I am” simply states that you exist and are in the world. The added “am I” flips the order, turning it into a question: “Am I …?” In philosophy, the most famous answer to a similar question is the famous phrase “I think, therefore I am.” It was used by René Descartes to show that the very act of questioning or thinking proves that there is a self that can think. So when you say “Am I am,” you’re essentially asking if the self that declares “I am” is real, and the answer, from both a common sense and a philosophical point of view, is yes—you do exist, and your very questioning proves that existence.
